record.title: India’s ESTIC 2026 draft vision reports Physical AI targets through 2047
record.summary: On 29 October 2026, the Press Information Bureau reported the release of the National Vision Document for India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026. Its account of the Department of Science and Technology’s autonomous-systems, Physical AI and robotics session describes recommendations to strengthen 25 National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems technology hubs for the mission’s next phase beginning in January 2028, build testbeds and India-specific datasets, support indigenous hardware with patient capital, and emphasize safety-by-design, hands-on training, early customer engagement and viable business models. PIB calls the proposed milestones a draft vision: pilot validation by 2030, wider deployment and manufacturing by 2035, and global competitiveness by 2047. A separate PIB release says stakeholder consultations had considered a possible Physical AI Mission. These sources do not establish an approved or funded mission, implementation owners, or delivered results; the full vision PDF was not located in this review.
organizations: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
Department of Science and Technology, Government of India
National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Press Information Bureau reported on 29 October 2026 that the National Vision Document for ESTIC 2026 and India STI Outlook 2026 were released.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: PIB reports that the Department of Science and Technology’s Physical AI session recommended strengthening 25 NM-ICPS hubs for a next phase beginning January 2028, testbeds, India-specific datasets, patient capital for indigenous hardware, hands-on training, safety-by-design, early customer engagement and viable business models; it describes pilot validation by 2030, wider deployment and manufacturing by 2035, and global competitiveness by 2047 as a draft vision.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A separate 29 October PIB release says stakeholder consultations had considered a proposal for a dedicated Physical AI Mission and suggests the next NM-ICPS phase could provide an opportunity to take it up.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected PIB releases do not establish that a dedicated Physical AI Mission or the reported draft milestones were formally approved, funded, assigned implementation owners, or achieved. The full National Vision Document was not directly inspected in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The complete released ESTIC 2026 National Vision Document was not located; the available PIB release summarizes its Physical AI section and labels the milestones draft.
No formal government order, budget, accountable delivery owner or procurement establishing an adopted Physical AI Mission or NM-ICPS Phase II programme was found.
No implementation, pilot-validation, deployment, manufacturing or global-competitiveness results are available in the inspected release.

brief.importance_rationale: If the draft programme is adopted and delivered, coordinating 25 cyber-physical technology hubs around testbeds, India-specific data, indigenous hardware and safety could materially influence India’s Physical AI research and industrial capacity. The score reflects that potential consequence; the official release describes draft milestones, not implementation.
limitations: The full National Vision Document was not located or directly inspected; detailed targets are attributed to PIB’s official summary.
The releases describe recommendations and a draft vision; they do not establish formal approval, dedicated budget, assigned owners, procurement, implementation or outcomes.
The possible Physical AI Mission appears as an idea considered in stakeholder consultations, not as an adopted mission.
organizations: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
Department of Science and Technology, Government of India
National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems

technical.claimed_result: PIB reports draft programme targets and recommendations for India’s Physical AI research and development, including strengthening 25 existing NM-ICPS hubs, testbeds and India-specific datasets, with a possible NM-ICPS next phase beginning Jan 2028.
technical.compute_or_cost: No Physical AI programme budget or cost is specified in the inspected releases. The phrase patient capital is a recommendation, not a quantified commitment.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official PIB publication event and its attributed account of a draft vision were directly inspected. No mission implementation, funded deployment, or resulting technical capability is demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: The reported approach would build on existing NM-ICPS technology hubs and connect research, testbeds, datasets, indigenous hardware finance, training, safety-by-design and customer engagement. The release does not specify an implementation architecture or accountable delivery owners.
technical.regime: India’s ESTIC 2026 policy and research-priority setting; draft national vision as summarized by PIB on 29 Oct 2026.
technical.reproducibility: The press-release statements are directly inspectable; the full National Vision PDF was not located. Independent policy adoption, budget and delivery evidence remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: PIB identifies 25 existing NM-ICPS technology hubs as the institutional baseline; the releases provide no measured capability, outcome or cost comparison.

brief.title: India’s ESTIC 2026 draft vision reports Physical AI targets through 2047
brief.why_it_matters: The reported draft vision connects India’s existing cyber-physical technology hubs to a long-horizon Physical AI programme, with proposals spanning test infrastructure, datasets, indigenous hardware finance and safety-by-design. If adopted and delivered, the milestones could shape research priorities and industrial capacity. The evidence here establishes what PIB reported, not adoption, funding, implementation or achieved capability.
